study_name.notes: No canonical study identifier/name given in the text.

subject_id.notes: No individual subject identifiers reported; only aggregate cohort data (n=35) provided.

sample_id.notes: No sample-level identifiers given; only aggregate library counts (70 sequencing libraries) reported.

curator.notes: Curator information not applicable/not present in paper text.

pmid.notes: PMID not stated within the body text of the paper itself.

subcohort.notes: No subcohort label given, though two travel destinations (Central Africa, Indian peninsula) exist as groupings.

target_condition.notes: Study examines gut microbiome/antibiotic resistance gene changes and ESBL acquisition after travel; no single named disease/condition phenotype is assigned to participants.

control.notes: Study design is a before/after longitudinal cohort, not a case-control design; no explicit case/control labeling.

country.evidence_quote: Swedish students from the universities in Umeå, Stockholm, and Gothenburg traveling for international exchange studies were invited
country.section: Methods — Subject selection and specimen collection
country.notes: Both before- and after-travel fecal specimens were collected in Sweden (before departure and after return to Sweden).

body_site.evidence_quote: fecal specimens from 35 Swedish students taken before and after exchange programs

days_from_first_collection.notes: Only aggregate medians/ranges for collection timing reported (e.g., median 4 days before departure, 22 days after return); no per-sample day values.

location.evidence_quote: Swedish students from the universities in Umeå, Stockholm, and Gothenburg traveling for international exchange studies
location.section: Methods — Subject selection and specimen collection

westernized.evidence_quote: Swedish students from the universities in Umeå, Stockholm, and Gothenburg
westernized.section: Methods — Subject selection and specimen collection
westernized.notes: Inferred from participants being Swedish university students in Sweden (a high-income, industrialized/westernized nation); not explicitly labeled 'westernized' in text.

antibiotics_exclusion_period.evidence_quote: None of the subjects included were allowed to have taken antibiotics within 6 months prior to fecal sampling.
antibiotics_exclusion_period.section: Methods — Subject selection and specimen collection

antibiotics_exclusion_period_unit.evidence_quote: None of the subjects included were allowed to have taken antibiotics within 6 months prior to fecal sampling.
antibiotics_exclusion_period_unit.section: Methods — Subject selection and specimen collection

dna_extraction_kit.notes: Main text states 'DNA was extracted from the fecal specimens' without naming a kit; kit details may be in supplemental methods not provided.

ncbi_accession.evidence_quote: Sequence data have been submitted to the European Nucleotide Archive under accession number PRJEB7369.
ncbi_accession.notes: ENA accession (not NCBI SRA specifically), but represents the deposited sequence data accession.

sequencing_platform.evidence_quote: DNA was extracted from the fecal specimens and sequenced using Illumina HiSeq 2000 technology.
sequencing_platform.section: Methods — Subject selection and specimen collection
sequencing_platform.notes: A separate platform (Illumina MiSeq, 250-bp paired-end) was used for sequencing ESBL-positive bacterial isolates, not the fecal metagenomic samples.

age.evidence_quote: Subjects were 23 to 34 years old, with a gender distribution of 74% females (26/35).
age.notes: Reported as an age range for the whole cohort, not per-subject ages; no mean/median age given.

age_group.notes: Age range 23-34 falls within Adult category (>=18 & <65 years).

ancestry.notes: Nationality (Swedish) is given but ancestry/ethnicity is not explicitly discussed.

sex.notes: Only an aggregate cohort-level sex distribution (74% female, 26/35) is reported, not per-subject sex; cannot assign a single enum value without fabricating individual-level data.

zigosity.notes: Not applicable to this study population.

age_min.notes: Reported as a range for the entire cohort (n=35), not individual ages.

age_max.notes: Reported as a range for the entire cohort (n=35), not individual ages.

age_years.notes: Only an age range (23-34 years) is given, no specific individual ages or mean.

antibiotics_current_use.evidence_quote: None of the subjects included were allowed to have taken antibiotics within 6 months prior to fecal sampling.
antibiotics_current_use.section: Methods — Subject selection and specimen collection
antibiotics_current_use.notes: Applies to entire cohort; also stated 'since none of the subjects took antibiotics before or during travel' in Discussion.

disease.evidence_quote: Swedish students from the universities in Umeå, Stockholm, and Gothenburg traveling for international exchange studies
disease.section: Methods — Subject selection and specimen collection
disease.notes: No explicit health status statement; inferred as healthy since subjects are described as students without antibiotics use and no disease/condition is mentioned.

disease_response_orr.notes: Not applicable; this is not an oncology treatment-response study.

feces_phenotype.notes: Traveler's diarrhea is mentioned as an event during travel but no formal stool phenotype/measurement is reported.

fmt_id.notes: Not applicable; not an FMT study.

treatment.evidence_quote: All travelers to Central Africa and 44% (8/18) of travelers to the Indian peninsula used antimalarial chemoprophylaxis.
treatment.notes: Usage varied by destination (100% Central Africa, 44% Indian peninsula); not a per-subject treatment given at study_level granularity.

tumor_staging_ajcc.notes: Not applicable; not an oncology study.

biomarker_name.notes: These are the three antibiotic resistance gene categories with the most prominent fold-change increases reported.

value: 35 Swedish health care students traveled to Indian peninsula (n=18) or Central Africa (n=17) for exchange programs

All CTX-M-15 positive E. coli isolates carried this ESBL gene
